beginner.problemText:
A college surveys students about how they usually travel to campus. Each student either usually uses public transit or does not. In a sample of 240 students, 138 students said they usually use public transit to get to campus.

The college wants to estimate the true percentage, or population proportion, of all students who usually use public transit to get to campus. Use an appropriate z-based method to make a 95% confidence interval for this population proportion. Also write one sentence that explains the interval in this campus travel context.
linguisticNotes: Uses short, direct sentences and familiar student-life wording.
Introduces “percentage” before “population proportion” to support accessibility.
States the success outcome plainly: a student usually uses public transit to get to campus.
Keeps the statistical task explicit without giving computational details or results.

intermediate.problemText:
A college surveys students about how they usually travel to campus. In a sample of 240 students, 138 reported that they usually use public transit to get to campus.

Construct a 95% confidence interval for the population proportion of students at the college who usually use public transit to get to campus. Include a brief interpretation of the interval in context.
linguisticNotes: Uses standard introductory statistics wording, including “sample,” “confidence interval,” and “population proportion.”
Keeps the sample size and number of successes clear in paragraph form.
Does not state the computed sample proportion, leaving that calculation to the student.
Avoids an explicit method prompt while preserving the two-sided confidence interval task.

advanced.problemText: In a student transportation survey, 138 of 240 sampled students indicated that they usually use public transit to get to campus. Treating this binary response as the success outcome, construct a 95% confidence interval for the population proportion of students who usually use public transit to get to campus. Provide a concise contextual interpretation of the resulting interval.
linguisticNotes: Uses compact statistical phrasing appropriate for an upper-level or scientific register.
Frames the response as a binary outcome and identifies the success outcome naturally.
Preserves the sample evidence and confidence level without reporting the computed sample proportion.
Foregrounds inference for the population proportion while leaving the procedure and computations to the student.
